note: The keeper's own pages (docs/future/13 section 2.4), written in the walker's hand and kept in the journal: the first opens by itself at the spring on the first evening. Each is { id, form, title, body: [lines] } in the letters' light markup (src/ui/journal-letters.js); an empty line starts a new paragraph. Under 60 words each. The first page's text is a stand-in until the story collaborator's arrives. The second (tend) shows as a centered card when you wake from your first rest (or at the first dawn, for a player who never rested), one click closes it, and it is kept here after the first (Phase 1 fix F15; stand-in text, words approved October 25, 2026, until the story collaborator's arrive). Set pieces add their pages here (docs/future/14; src/world/setpieces/live.js sets keeper:<id> when one is due): the cairns and the old keeper's letter under the last cairn, the passing boat, and the boat's letters (form From the boat, had as each gift is taken up; their order in recipes/setpieces/boat.json). words.entryLine: In your own hand, from the morning you came.
words.entryLineMany: In your own hand, since the morning you came.
words.title: Keeper's pages

pages.title: The first page
body: I came in on the morning tide. The land here is new, still pale from the sea.
Keepers don't own the islands we tend. We help them hold what comes, and write down what we see.
Someone will read this after me. Start at the spring.

pages.title: What a keeper does
body: A keeper doesn't build. A keeper tends.
Shape the land and let the tide shape it back. Make room for water, plants and shelter, and the creatures will find it, each in its own time.
The island grows while you are away: ebb, and flow, and ebb again.

pages.title: The cairns
body: They came one at a time, at dawn, all that spring. Flat stones, stacked by someone careful. I never saw who.

body.line: I added a stone to one, and the next morning's cairn had one more. Someone was answering.
I left them as I found them. Each leaned toward the next, and I followed.

body: At the end, a letter. I have left them standing.

pages.title: Under the last stone
body: If you are reading this, you followed them all the way. Good. Most never look up from the ground long enough.
I kept this island before you. It kept me, really.
Leave the cairns standing. Someone likes to know the way is still marked.

pages.title: The lantern on the water
body: A boat lay off the island at dusk, a lantern at its stern, a bell when the swell moved it. It never came closer.

body.line: I left a parcel on the flat stone by the mooring. By morning the boat was gone, and something lay there in its place.
I watched until the lamp went out. By morning it was gone.

body: Whoever they are, they know this shore has a keeper now.

pages.title: A note, in pencil
body: Thank you for the parcel. We don't stop often. The lamp on your shore was the only one for miles.
Seeds, for whatever ground you have.

pages.title: A second note
body: Your herbs kept the whole crossing. The cook asks what the yellow ones were.
We'll look for your light again.

pages.title: A note, folded small
body: We had weather off the point last week, and thought of you out there.
Whatever you sent, it smelled of your island. Here is some cord, the good kind.

pages.title: A longer note
body: We've started keeping your notes in a tin by the wheel.
When the wind is right we can see your fire from the channel. It is a strange comfort, a fire with no town around it.

pages.title: A note, in a careful hand
body: The young one aboard draws your island now, from what you send. Shells along the bottom, a heron in the corner.
Tell us if we have it wrong.

pages.title: A note, with a pressed flower
body: A flower from where we put in, for your journal.
We count the seasons by your stone now. Spring, and the lamp on the shore. Summer, and the lamp.

pages.title: A note, the paper soft
body: You never ask anything of us, so we've stopped asking what to send. We just send what we would want, if we were you.
Keep well out there.

pages.title: A note, tied with cord
body: This is for keeping: the last of a coil that has been aboard longer than any of us.
Use it for something that should last. We are thinking of your island.

pages.title: A short note
body: All well aboard. The light on your shore is still the first we look for.

pages.title: A short note
body: Fair weather this crossing. Thank you, as ever.

pages.title: A short note
body: The tin by the wheel is nearly full. We'll need a second.
